choices.purpose: States that CRP results alone must not drive decisions to stop antibiotics
choices.quote: Do not use C-reactive protein results alone to make decisions about starting, continuing or stopping antibiotics.

choices.purpose: Provides the full set of criteria for stopping antibiotics at 36 h, showing CRP is only one component
choices.quote: stop antibiotics at 36 hours if: • the blood culture is negative and • the initial clinical suspicion of infection was not strong and • the baby's clinical condition is reassuring, with no clinical indicators of possible infection … and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration are reassuring.

choices.purpose: Describes how CRP should be used together with other data to assess infection likelihood and treatment response
choices.quote: Measure baseline C-reactive protein concentration when starting antibiotic treatment in babies who may have neonatal infection. Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment.
